# Tests that cannot run unattended, excluded from every automated tier rather than skipped.
#
# One list, read by `.github/scripts/hardware-only-skips.sh` and applied by every workflow that tests the
# `PayabliSDK-Package` scheme. This file does not name them, because a roster written here goes stale the
# first time one is added and it did: `verify.py` finds them by reading the workflow directory instead,
# and asserts each one applies this list. The release build is among them and it tags, so an exclusion
# missing there ships. Two copies of the list would be two lists the moment one of them is edited, and the
# failure mode is silent — a test excluded in one tier and skipping in the other reports a standing skip
# nobody reads.
#
# Why excluded rather than skipped: the reporter derives passed from total minus failed minus skipped, so a
# test parked with `XCTSkip` reports a skip every night, and a permanent skip cannot be told apart from a
# regression that started skipping. An excluded test is absent from the result bundle and the counts stay
# honest.
#
# The bar is that the test would fail or answer wrongly unattended, not that nobody has taught the
# automation to run it. The second is a provisioning gap, fixed by changing a workflow rather than by owning
# a device, and a test parked here for that reason is borrowing time.
#
# A whole suite that needs hardware belongs in its own test target instead, which is what the sample app's
# DeviceTests and UITests bundles are. This file is for a class or a method inside a target that otherwise
# runs. Entries are `Target/Class` or `Target/Class/method`, without parentheses. Blank lines and anything
# after a `#` are ignored.

# Need a Keychain that answers. The Swift package test host carries no entitlement, so these return
# errSecMissingEntitlement and skipped on every simulator run before this list existed. The other ten
# tests in SecureStorageTests run normally, which is why these are named per method.
#
# Every assertion here has a counterpart in PayabliDemoDeviceTests/KeychainOnDeviceTests, which skips
# nothing. Two of them did not until this list was reviewed: the update path of `set` on an item that
# already exists, and the sweep creating no item for any key it knows. The device suite covered the add
# path and the sweep's correction, which are different branches, so excluding those two would have
# dropped the only test of each. Check the counterpart exists before adding a line here; "it is covered
# on a device" is a claim about a file, and it was wrong twice.
PayabliSDKTapToPayTests/SecureStorageTests/testKeychainRoundTripIfAvailable
PayabliSDKTapToPayTests/SecureStorageTests/testKeychainItemsAreWrittenForThisDeviceOnlyIfAvailable
PayabliSDKTapToPayTests/SecureStorageTests/testRewritingALegacyItemStopsItTravellingIfAvailable
PayabliSDKTapToPayTests/SecureStorageTests/testTheSweepRewritesAStoredItemAndKeepsItsValueIfAvailable
PayabliSDKTapToPayTests/SecureStorageTests/testTheSweepStoresNothingForAKeyThatHasNoItemIfAvailable
